title: Reflect (flip) a shape over a line

lesson.title: Flip It Over the Line!

steps.say: You already know how to find a line of symmetry, where one half of a shape matches the other half perfectly. Today we use that same idea to make the matching half ourselves. That is called a reflection, or a flip.

Here is the big rule for flipping. Pick one corner of your shape. Count how many steps it is from the mirror line. Then go the same number of steps to the other side of the line. Same distance, opposite side. It is like standing in front of a mirror at the pool in Burnaby. If you stand two metres from the mirror, your reflection looks like it is two metres behind it.

visual.caption: Corner A sits at two right, three up

steps.say: Let us flip a real triangle. Our mirror line is the up and down line at x equals four. Corner A is at two, three. Count from two over to four. That is two steps. Now go two more steps past the line, to six. So A lands at six, three. Notice the up and down number, three, does not change at all. We only slid sideways across the line.

visual.caption: A at two, three flips to six, three across the line x equals four

steps.say: Now the other two corners. Corner B is at three, one. From three to four is one step, so go one step past the line, to five. B lands at five, one. Corner C is at one, one. From one to four is three steps, so go three steps past, to seven. C lands at seven, one. Every corner keeps its same height and hops across.

visual.caption: B at three, one goes to five, one. C at one, one goes to seven, one

steps.say: Here is the mistake I see most often. Some kids just slide the whole triangle to the right, keeping it facing the same way. That is a slide, not a flip. Watch corner C. In a slide, C would still be on the left side of the triangle. But in a real flip, C ends up farthest to the right, at seven, one, because the shape turns around like a mirror image. If your flipped shape looks exactly like the original just moved over, you slid it instead of flipping it.

visual.caption: C was left of B, but after the flip C is right of B — the order swaps

steps.say: So remember, for every single corner, count to the line, then count the same amount past it. Same distance, other side, and the shape turns around.

lesson.answer: To flip a shape, move every corner the same distance to the other side of the mirror line — the shape turns around, it does not just slide.

practice.question: On a coordinate grid, Maya draws a flag for the Canada Day parade. The two corners of her flag are at two, five and three, two. Her mirror line is the up and down line at x equals six. Draw the grid yourself and find where those two corners land after the flip.
practice.answer: The corner at two, five lands at ten, five, because two is four steps from six, so it goes four steps past to ten. The corner at three, two lands at nine, two, because three is three steps from six, so it goes three steps past to nine. Both keep their same height.
